community: Our street is a friendly community where neighbours share garden tools.
Everyone in our village, young and old, joined the community litter pick.
A school is a small community of teachers and children.
government: Mum works for the government, planning where new railways should go.
individual: Every child is a special individual with their own ideas.
Each individual in the choir sang a different note.
Only one individual can sit on the swing at a time.
marvellous: What a marvellous rainbow stretched across the sky!
We had a marvellous day building sandcastles at the seaside.
Did you have a marvellous time at the zoo yesterday?
mischievous: The mischievous puppy hid my slipper under the sofa.
My little brother gave a mischievous grin and hid the remote.
The mischievous wind blew my hat right off my head!
parliament: A new law must be voted on in parliament first.
Members of parliament meet to talk about new laws.
In parliament, the members debate and vote on new laws.
profession: What profession would you like to have when you grow up?
Teaching is a hard profession that needs years of training.
My uncle trained for years to learn his profession as an engineer.
opportunity: The sunny weekend was a perfect opportunity for a picnic.
I jumped at the opportunity to feed the ducks at the park.
Will I get another opportunity to ride the big slide?
programme: We watched a nature programme about hedgehogs after tea.
The school play programme lists every song in order.
Mum wrote a programme of games for the birthday party.
guarantee: Nobody can guarantee that the sun will shine on sports day.
Can you guarantee that you will feed the cat every morning?
I guarantee I will bring your pencil back tomorrow.

rejected.s: Our prime minister is the leader of the government.
rejected.reason: checker: A child could easily think the prime minister leads parliament. (also fits: parliament)

rejected.s: The government decided to plant more trees along every road in the country.
rejected.reason: checker: Parliament could also decide something for the whole country. (also fits: parliament)

rejected.s: Who is in charge of the government in Britain?
rejected.reason: checker: 'In charge of parliament' fits the gap just as well. (also fits: parliament)

rejected.s: The government sent a letter to every home about the new bins!
rejected.reason: checker: Bins are a local matter, so a community letter could fit too. (also fits: community)

rejected.s: Can you name the individual who won the egg race?
rejected.reason: checker: 'Egg race' is not natural UK English; it should be 'egg and spoon race'.
